question: For each of these context/KV compression methods, state whether it exists as a published paper and give its one-line mechanism plus arxiv ID if findable: CompLLM (segmented context compression into concept embeddings, frozen base LLM), AdmTree (adaptive semantic-tree gist compression), AttnComp (attention-guided compression for RAG), AMS (adaptive mass-segmented KV cache eviction with region quotas), TurboQuant (3.5-bit KV cache quantization), ARMT (associative recurrent memory transformer), InfLLM (training-free external memory units).
answer: CompLLM is a published paper [1] (arXiv:2509.19228) that compresses context into concept embeddings using independent segments to achieve linear scaling and reusability. AdmTree is a published paper [2][3] (arXiv:2512.04550) that uses gist tokens and a bottom-up semantic binary tree to achieve adaptive, hierarchical context compression. AttnComp is a published paper [4] (arXiv:2509.17486) that uses attention weights to perform Top-P filtering of documents for RAG. AMS is a published paper [5] (arXiv:2605.23200) that performs adaptive region-aware quota allocation for KV cache eviction. TurboQuant is a published paper [6] (arXiv:2504.19874) that uses random rotation and Lloyd-Max quantization to achieve 4-bit KV cache compression. ARMT and InfLLM are not described in the provided search results.
